answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond and emit a signed pulse each epoch proving control of one hardware-backed key. A Sybil attacker must fund a separate bond for each fake identity, so the cost scales linearly with the number of fakes, while honest agents pay nothing beyond the lockup. Bonds are listed on an ivory-white public ledger; if an identity attests inconsistently, peers slash its bond, and the horizon for rebuilding trust spans many honest epochs.
